evidence.quoted_text:
"manager_restarted": (
            (((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
             .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                 .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            and bool(((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and bool(((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")),
evidence.reason: The manager_restarted predicate compares only manager PID and invocation ID. It never requires the manager before/after snapshots to share a nonempty boot ID, so a guest reboot between the two inspects can change both PID and invocation ID and still make manager_restarted true. That confounds the isolated manager-restart result with a reboot; the separate boot_id_changed check covers the reboot snapshot pair, not the manager snapshot pair. Requiring nonempty equal boot IDs in the manager snapshots while keeping the existing PID and invocation-ID inequality checks is the smallest compatible correctness fix.
